data.claim: plan_edit runs on the _load snapshot outside log.transaction(); a concurrent claim between the fold and _record_update's append is not caught
data.falsifier: I.update(...) exits 0 and records the change when another agent claims between the snapshot and the append
data.mechanism: update() plans from st at _load; _record_update appends under the lock without re-checking; only _update_and_rebind re-folds, and only for the rebind decision

data.question: Does update validate its coordination checks (line frozen, claimed parent) against the log as it is when the edit appends?

evidence.note: Rb21b034a80 CONFIRMED: plan_edit ran on the _load snapshot outside the lock. Probe on the unfixed tree (ci pre-push): tests/test_update_plan_locked.py 2 failed -- update recorded line='1' / parent='A' after a concurrent claim (exit 0, must be REFUSED). r-small-files: both files <20KB; r-everything-configurable: no new tunables; r-reuse-core: reused plan_edit/_record_update/_update_and_rebind and batch.apply's plan-under-lock pattern, no new machinery; commit trailers clean (no Co-Authored-By).

ddflow/api/items.py update(): plan_edit + landed + record now inside ONE log.transaction() with a fresh L._fold, mirroring batch.apply and _update_and_rebind; concurrent claim/move between snapshot and append is refused. Regression tests tests/test_update_plan_locked.py (2 tests) fail on the unfixed tree, pass fixed: unit_tests gate PASSED 2274 passed.

chunk_findings.detail: When `edit.worktree` is set, `update` now enters `log.transaction()` and then calls `_update_and_rebind(...)`. The change’s own description states that `_update_and_rebind` already “re-folds inside the lock,” i.e. it acquires `log.transaction()` itself. This diff therefore nests the same exclusive log transaction: an update such as `ddflow update task --worktree wt` acquires the log lock in `update`, then `_update_and_rebind`’s inner `with log.transaction():` must wait for the lock already held by the outer frame. With a non-reentrant transaction/lock context manager this deadlocks/hangs the worktree update path; the added regression tests cover `--line` and `--parent` but not `--worktree`, so the failure is not caught. This also risks the advisory [r-lock-cycle-selfheal] by holding a lock while waiting for it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/items.py:update (worktree branch)

chunk_findings.detail: Both race tests inject a mutating CLI command into `_load`: `load_then_someone_claims` runs `ddflow claim ...` after reading the fold. The fix’s purpose is to perform this fold *inside* `log.transaction()`, i.e. while the update transaction holds the inter-process log lock. When the monkeypatched `_load` invokes `claim`, that CLI command must acquire the same log lock to append its claim event. The parent `update` call is waiting for `_load` to return and therefore cannot release the lock, while the child `claim` waits for the lock; the test deadlocks/hangs (or times out and the inner `assert ... == OK` fails) instead of reaching the expected `REFUSED` assertion. This is a hold-while-waiting circular wait, also contrary to [r-lock-cycle-selfheal].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_update_plan_locked.py:39 and :59

data.probe: log.transaction() IS reentrant by depth count keyed on (pid, lock path): infra/log.py:1098-1122; the same nesting already exists today (_update_and_rebind holds transaction() while calling _record_update's own with log.transaction(), items.py:223-230) and delete semantics are explicit there. The worktree path is exercised: tests/test_sticky_binding.py::test_update_worktree_rebinds_the_item_and_the_lease and 10 other stub tests pass in the unit_tests gate run (2274 passed).

data.probe: update() calls the patched _load ONCE, OUTSIDE (before) log.transaction(); inside the lock it refolds with L._fold(log), never _load (items.py:83-91 fixed). The nested claim subprocess holds no lock the parent waits on. The tests pass on the fixed tree and complete in seconds (unit_tests gate evidence).

update() calls the patched _load ONCE, OUTSIDE (before) log.transaction(); inside the lock it refolds with L._fold(log), never _load (items.py:83-91 fixed). The nested claim subprocess holds no lock the parent waits on. The tests pass on the fixed tree and complete in seconds (unit_tests gate evidence).

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test’s monkeypatched `_load` invokes `run_cli(repo, "claim", ...)` from inside the fold itself. The fix being tested requires the coordination fold to be taken inside `log.transaction()`. When the fixed `update` path calls `_load` under the log lock, the patched `_load` will run the `claim` CLI while the outer process already holds that lock; `claim` must acquire the same log lock to append, so the test will block/deadlock (or time out) instead of passing. A one-shot race cannot be simulated by globally patching `_load` to perform a locking CLI command; this also violates the advisory against holding while waiting [r-lock-cycle-selfheal].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_update_plan_locked.py:33

data.probe: Same premise as the refuted rubber_duck #2: in the fixed update(), _load runs BEFORE log.transaction() opens (items.py:83-91); inside the lock the code refolds with L._fold(log) and never calls _load, so the patched _load's run_cli claim subprocess takes and releases the log lock while update holds nothing. The tests complete and assert REFUSED (unit_tests gate: passed, 2274). The nested transaction on the worktree branch is reentrant by design (infra/log.py:1105-1108 keyed on pid+lock path) and that nesting already exists on main (_update_and_rebind holds transaction() across _record_update's own transaction(), items.py:223-230).
